text:
Sean Couturier is the Flyers' captain, a former Selke winner, and right now a 33-year-old trying to find his finish. He has one goal in 22 games on 4.2% shooting, and after a 3-2 overtime loss in Calgary he summed up the team's month to NBC Sports Philadelphia: the Flyers were "finding ways to lose".

The bigger concern is the play, not the finish. Philadelphia gets only 43% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, and his own chance rate (0.46 expected goals per 60) is down from 0.68 last season. His minutes have dipped by almost two a night over his last ten games. Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports flagged a costly breakout turnover against Edmonton.

The defensive reputation still holds up in the long view: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.17 fewer expected goals per 60 with him on last season, 96th percentile among forwards. He kills penalties and moves the puck more than he shoots. Our range has him scoring more than this, but probably closer to 10 goals than 20. For a captain on a rebuilding team, the job now might be more shutdown center than scorer.
